title: Prompt Engineering Basics
description: The same AI model can produce wildly different outputs depending on how you ask. This lesson teaches you the four components of an effective prompt — and why they matter.
learningObjectives: Explain what a prompt is and why it shapes AI output
Identify the four components of an effective prompt
Write a basic prompt that includes task, context, and constraints
Recognize weak vs strong prompts in real examples

opening.hook: You have probably typed something like 'Tell me about AI' into ChatGPT. You got an answer — but was it useful? Probably not. The problem was not the AI. The problem was the prompt. The same model, given a better prompt, would have given you a much better response.
opening.relevance: Prompt engineering is the difference between using AI as a toy and using AI as a tool.

content.content: A prompt is the input you give to an AI system to guide its response. It can be a question, an instruction, a description, or a combination of all three.

content.definition: Any text input given to an AI model that shapes the model's output.
content.example: 'Explain gravity in one paragraph' is a prompt. 'What is gravity?' is also a prompt — but a weaker one.

content.content: Here is the key insight: AI models are probabilistic. They do not retrieve a specific answer from a database. They generate responses based on patterns learned from training data. The prompt determines which patterns get activated.

content.title: Why this matters
content.content: A vague prompt activates many patterns, producing a generic answer. A specific prompt activates the right patterns, producing a useful answer.

sections.title: The Four Components of a Good Prompt

content.content: Effective prompts usually include four key elements. You do not always need all four — but knowing them helps you diagnose why a prompt is not working.

content.definition: What you want the AI to do — summarize, translate, explain, generate, classify.
content.example: 'Summarize this article' is a task. 'Explain this concept' is a task.

content.definition: Background information the AI needs to understand the request.
content.example: 'For a beginner audience' or 'In a business context' provides context.

content.definition: Rules or boundaries on the output — length, tone, things to avoid.
content.example: 'In under 100 words' or 'Avoid technical jargon' are constraints.

content.definition: How you want the output structured — bullet points, paragraphs, JSON, table.
content.example: 'Return as a bulleted list' specifies format.

content.after: Strong: 'Explain what AI is in 3 bullet points for a 10-year-old, avoiding technical jargon.'

content.content: Notice how the strong prompt contains all four components: Task (explain), Context (for a 10-year-old), Constraints (avoid jargon), Format (3 bullet points).

Prompt engineering is not a one-shot activity. The first prompt rarely produces the optimal result. Experienced prompt engineers treat each prompt as a hypothesis: 'If I say this, will the model do that?'

content.title: Iterative prompt refinement
steps: Prompt 2: 'Explain quantum computing to a high school student.'
Response: Better, but still uses unexplained terms.
Prompt 3: 'Explain quantum computing to a high school student in 3 short paragraphs, avoiding equations, with one real-world example.'

content.title: The skill is in the refinement
content.content: You do not need to write perfect prompts. You need to be able to look at a bad response and diagnose why — then refine.

content.myth: There is one perfect prompt for every task.
content.reality: Prompts depend on the model, the context, and the learner's goal. What works for one model may fail for another.

keyTakeaways: A prompt is the input that shapes AI output.
Effective prompts have four components: Task, Context, Constraints, Format.
Vague prompts produce generic answers. Specific prompts produce useful answers.
Prompt engineering is iterative — refine until you get the output you need.

reflection.prompt: Think about a prompt you have used recently. Which of the four components was missing?
reflection.hint: Most people forget Context or Constraints.
reflection.expectedInsight: Identifying the missing component helps you improve your next prompt immediately.

flashcards.back: Any text input given to an AI model that shapes its output.

flashcards.front: What are the four components of an effective prompt?
Why do vague prompts produce generic answers?
flashcards.back: Because they activate many patterns, producing an unfocused response.
Because AI is probabilistic — first prompts rarely produce optimal results.

items.question: In the prompt 'Summarize this article for a busy executive in 5 bullet points', which part is the CONSTRAINT?
items.explanation: 'In 5 bullet points' is a constraint on the output — it limits the length and format.
items.whyItMatters: Identifying components helps you diagnose why a prompt is not producing useful output.

items.question: Which prompt is strongest?
options: Explain the main causes of climate change in 3 short paragraphs for a high school student, avoiding political opinions
items.explanation: This prompt includes all four components: Task (explain), Context (for a high school student), Constraints (3 paragraphs, avoid politics), Format (short paragraphs).
items.whyItMatters: This shows how the same underlying question becomes dramatically more useful with structure.

items.question: Rewrite this prompt to include at least 3 of the 4 components: 'Tell me about ChatGPT.'
items.answer: Example: 'Explain what ChatGPT is in 3 short bullet points for someone who has never used an AI tool before, avoiding technical jargon.'
items.explanation: A strong rewrite adds Context (never used AI), Constraints (avoid jargon), and Format (3 bullet points).
items.whyItMatters: This is the core skill: taking a vague request and adding structure.

items.question: You ask an AI for a summary of a long report. The response is 800 words — way too long. Which component of your prompt was missing?
items.answer: Constraints. You did not specify a length limit or format. Adding 'in under 100 words' or 'as 5 bullet points' would fix the issue.
items.explanation: When output is too long or too vague, the most common cause is missing constraints.
items.whyItMatters: Diagnosing a bad output is the first step to fixing the prompt.

notes.summary: Prompts shape AI output. Effective prompts include Task, Context, Constraints, and Format. Prompt engineering is an iterative skill.
keyPoints: Prompt = input text that guides AI output
Four components: Task, Context, Constraints, Format
Iteration is part of the process

importantTerms.definition: Input text given to an AI model.
A rule or boundary on the output.

notes.reflection: Prompt engineering is a learnable skill, not a talent.
